question: Should ClawSweeper adopt public exact-review queue telemetry as a production scheduling input with broad-worker ceilings of 16 when congested and 4 when saturated?
rationale: Tests can verify classification mechanics, but they cannot decide the desired fleet-allocation policy or acceptable background-throughput tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt after proof
options.body: Keep the 16/4 policy, require conflict resolution and a live scheduler transcript, then review the exact rebased head.

options.title: Tune the ceilings
options.body: Choose different congestion and saturation limits based on the desired minimum broad-review and commit-review throughput.

options.title: Decline telemetry coupling
options.body: Keep scheduling based only on currently counted active work and close the PR if public dashboard telemetry should not influence admission.

recommendation.title: Adopt after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the 16/4 policy, require conflict resolution and a live scheduler transcript, then review the exact rebased head.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a production fleet-allocation and automation-policy choice rather than a mechanically provable code correction.
